title: Where Does Warm-Up Come From? Adaptive Scheduling for Norm-Constrained Optimizers
claim: Local curvature measured along real optimization trajectories grows quadratically with the suboptimality gap, empirically supporting the generalized smoothness assumption.
layout: single scatter plot with colorbar on right, red fitted curve, legend with R2
description: A single large scatter plot. The x-axis is the suboptimality gap Δ^t = loss(x^t) − loss*, running from about 0.6 to 5. The y-axis is a smoothness ratio, a gradient-difference norm divided by the step norm, on a 1e8 scale. Many points form a rising, curved band. A thick red quadratic fit, K0 + K1·Δ + K2·Δ², runs through them. A legend at top left gives the formula and R2 = 0.973. Points are colored by training iteration using a blue-to-red coolwarm colorbar on the right, from about 1000 to 8000. Early iterations are blue and sit at large Δ and high ratio. Late iterations are red and cluster tightly near the bottom left, with low Δ and low ratio. The eye goes first to the red curve and the upward-sweeping blue cloud.
caption: Empirical smoothness ratio $\mathcal{K}^t$ versus suboptimality gap $\Delta^t$ for Lion on large-scale pretraining. The trajectory is well-fitted by a quadratic dependence, indicating $K_\rho > 0$. All hyperparameter setup is provided in Appendix [ref].
abstract: We study adaptive learning rate scheduling for norm-constrained optimizers (e.g., Muon and Lion). We introduce a generalized smoothness assumption under which local curvature decreases with the suboptimality gap and empirically verify that this behavior holds along optimization trajectories. Under this assumption, we establish convergence guarantees under an appropriate choice of learning rate, for which warm-up followed by decay arises naturally from the proof rather than being imposed heuristically. Building on this theory, we develop a practical learning rate scheduler that relies only on standard hyperparameters and adapts the warm-up duration automatically at the beginning of training. We evaluate this method on large language model pretraining with LLaMA architectures and show that our adaptive warm-up selection consistently outperforms or at least matches the best manually tuned warm-up schedules across all considered setups, without additional hyperparameter search. Our source code is available at https://github.com/brain-lab-research/llm-baselines/tree/warmup
